hero: In the living room of a modest concrete house in Zamboanga City, a Filipino nephrology fellow and a PD nurse kneel beside a seated middle-aged Filipino man with a peritoneal dialysis bag hanging from a hook, the nurse holding a drained bag to the window light while the man's wife holds the exchange notebook; boxes of solution stacked by the wall, warm afternoon light, no text in image.

figures.teaches: Ultrafiltration in PD rises then falls because glucose is absorbed through the same pores that let water in.
figures.content: Left panel: cross-section of a peritoneal capillary between blood (left) and peritoneal cavity (right) through interstitium and mesothelium. Capillary wall shows three labeled pathways: 'Small pores (radius 40-55 Å; ~99% of pore area; water + small solutes)', 'Large pores (radius ~250 Å; ~0.01%; proteins)', 'Water-only pores (aquaporin-1; ~2% of UF coefficient; water without sodium)'. Arrows: water moving blood -> cavity through small pores and aquaporins (blue), urea and creatinine diffusing blood -> cavity (orange), glucose diffusing cavity -> blood (green), lymphatic reabsorption cavity -> lymph vessel (gray). Right panel: graph of net ultrafiltration (mL) vs dwell time (0-10 h) with two curves: 'Low transporter' rising and staying positive; 'High transporter' peaking early (~2 h) and falling below zero by the end of a long dwell; dashed curve 'Icodextrin long dwell' staying positive. Callout 'Sodium sieving: dialysate sodium dips in hour 1'. Footer '© renalcarematters.com'.

figures.teaches: PET transport category predicts clearance and long-dwell ultrafiltration and guides prescription direction.
figures.content: Graph A: D/P creatinine (y, 0 to 1.0) vs time (0, 1, 2, 4 h), four bands labeled High, High-average, Low-average, Low. Graph B: D/D0 glucose (y, 1.0 down) vs time, mirror image bands. Marker on the High band at 4 h labeled 'Case: 0.85 (unit reference: high)'. Bottom strip table: High = fast clearance, poor long-dwell UF -> shorter dwells (APD), icodextrin long dwell; Average = standard CAPD or APD to goals; Low = slow clearance, good UF -> longer dwells, larger fills. Note 'Meta-analysis: RR 1.15 for death per 0.1 rise in D/P creatinine (observational)'. Footer '© renalcarematters.com'.
